- **Items:** 8 techniques, numbered unevenly ("my first", "my next", "my second"). Shortest: item 2, shapewear (132 words, 55 seconds); longest: item 5, asymmetry (404 words, 2:58). Typical 150 to 360 words. Item one starts at 0:32, after 77 words (4% of the video). Order: the foundations under the clothes first, then colour, fabric and line principles, then single garments (tops, trousers).
- **Item shape:** the look (the technique named), the why in optical terms (chops the body, clings and shines, points the eye at the tummy, adds bulk), a "no" example on screen, then a found "yes" example described feature by feature (darts, vertical seams, a V, a single row of buttons, full length) and a result in a fixed phrase ("10 lb thinner for sure"). Checks: get measured; long not cropped; look for the design in a structured fabric.
- **The title's promise:** "Look Slimmer" (0:09, and "10 lbs thinner" at 0:00, 5:49, 11:26, 16:05), "MOST EFFECTIVE" (not said), "Over 50" (not said in the speech; "as we grow older" at 1:35). Paid with eight concrete techniques.
- **Feelings:** 3 of 8 items name an inner feeling: item 1 (no shame in sizing up; you'll feel more comfortable, after), item 2 (uncomfortable in the heat, before), item 4 (you feel the fabric clinging, uncomfortable, before). The opening carries the main one: accept and love your body.
- **Villain:** the wrong underwear size, high-contrast blocks, cheap clingy fabric, a bad hem shape, elastic pleats and one brand of sandals. Habits and garments; never the viewer.
- **Hard words:** "catastrophically ugly" (15:17, about sandals, played for laughs); "lumps and bumps" (3:18, 6:19, 7:33); "droopier" (1:42). No "frumpy" or "old".
- **CTA placement:** a dress link at 13:22 (inside a 55-word objection answer) and the end-screen pointer at 16:12 (34 words). No subscribe, no sponsor.
- **Ending:** hopes you enjoyed the techniques that take ten pounds off your outline; the next video on screen. No recap.
- **What sets it apart from other models of its type:**
  - It opens with body acceptance before any trick, so slimming is framed as a choice of line, not a fix for a flaw.
  - Every technique is explained in optical terms (where the eye goes, where the body is "cut"), which makes the advice transferable to any garment.
  - Each "no" is paired with a "yes" described feature by feature, so the viewer learns what to look for on the label and the hanger.
  - **How she frames French women (for Diane's lens):** no claims about French women at all; only the French greeting. Her authority is "a professionally trained stylist" and a statistic ("many studies have shown"). Her hedges are about women in general ("many women", "the area you think is a problem for you"), never about a nation.

## Why it works

The opening line ("accept and love your body") disarms the slimming promise and drew the warmest comments: "I love this positive attitude because it stops us beating ourselves up for not being perfect." (32 likes). The why is optical and easy to remember (contrast chops you, a front-high hem points at the tummy), every no has a yes, and the jokes land: "Marianne, you are so funny and absolutely authentic, I love your sense of humour!" (288 likes); "made me laugh so much. I agree 100%" (163 likes). Viewers welcome the larger models: "So happy you use models that represent slightly larger people." (127 likes). Gaps: "None of these are for enlarged tummy. At menopause this is the hardest part of dressing." (83 likes); "I so wish elbow-length sleeves were popular again." (97 likes). A newer comment calls out the contradiction: "we all should love our body and then comes up with a bunch of suggestions to look slimmer" (0 likes). Changes: "wear more belts, have the courage to emphasize my figure and feel so much better!" (23 likes). The pace is slow (about 135 words a minute), with pauses for the pictures.
